secs.title: Section 3: Cost includes acquisition expenses like transfer charges, brokera
secs.text:
Cost includes acquisition expenses like transfer charges, brokerage, commission etc.

Excise duty

Liability for excise duty in respect of goods produces except for export. Provision is made for excisable manufactured goods as at the year end.

Fixed Assets

At the acquisition cost inclusive of inward freight, duties and taxes and incidental and direct expenses related to acquisition.

In respect of project involving construct, related pre-operational expenses including interest on specific loan prior to construction form part of cost of assets

Fixed assets received by way of non-monetary grant/other than towards corpus fund are capitalised at value stated by corresponding credit to capital reserve.

Depreciation

Straight-line Method as prescribed in Income Tax Act, 1961 (Illustrative) except depreciation on cost adjustment arising out of conversion of foreign exchange liability for acquisition of fixed assets.

Addition/deduction from fixed assets during the year on pro-rata basis

Assets costing Rs. 5000 or less, each are fully provided.

Deferred Revenue Exp.

Written over a period of 5 years from the year it is incurred

Sale Revenue

Sales include excise duty and are net of sales returns, rebate and trade discount

Grants/Subsidies

Contribution towards capital cost of setting up project-Capital reserve

In respect of specific fixed assets acquired-deduction from the cost of related assets

Accounted on realisation basis.

Foreign Currency Trans

Accounted at exchange rate prevailing at the date of transaction

Current assets, foreign currency loans and current liabilities are converted at the exchange rate prevailing at the year end.

Resultant gain/loss is adjusted to the cost of fixed assets, if relates to fixed assets else considered as revenue.

Lease

Lease rentals are considered expenses with reference to lease terms

Retirement Benefits

Liability towards death/retirement gratuity is accrued on the basis actuarial valuation.

Provision for accumulated leave encashment benefit to the employee is accrued and computed on assumption that employees are entitled to receive the benefit at the each year end.

Instructions and Accounting Principles

Basis

Preparation of financial statements on accrual based accounting and shall be in the form suggested or as near thereto as possible.

Disclosure

Disclosure of all significant accounting policies adopted for preparation of financial statements at one place.

Where any accounting policy is not in conformity with accounting standard and the effect of departure is material, such departure shall be disclosed.

Consistency

Accounting policies shall be applied consistently from one accounting year to another. Any change effect of which is material in current period or which is reasonably expected to have material effect in later period shall be disclosed.

Where financial impact is ascertainable, the amount shall also be disclosed. In other cases, full detail of the case shall be disclosed.

Objectivity

The accounting treatment and presentation, in financial statements, of transactions and events shall be governed by their substance and not merely by the legal form

Materiality

In determining the accounting treatment and manner of disclosure of an item in financial statement due consideration shall be given to the concept of materiality.

Prudence

Provision shall be made for all known liabilities and losses even though amount cannot be estimated with substantial accuracy.

Provision for contingent loss if it is probable that future events will confirm that an assets has been impaired or a liability has been incurred at the balance sheet date and a reasonable estimate of the amount of the resulting loss can be made.

In other cases, the existence of contingent loss shall be disclosed by way of a note to the income & expenditure account unless the possibility of the loss is remote.

Where any amount written off or retained by way of providing for depreciation, renewal or diminution in the value of assets or retained by way of providing for any known liability is in excess of amount which is considered reasonably necessary for the purpose, the excess shall be treated as a Reserve and not a Provision.

Revenue Recognition unless

The related performance has been achieved

No significant uncertainty exists regarding the amount of consideration

It is not unreasonable to expect realisation and ultimate collection.

Separate Disclosure

Prior-period items of income/expenditure of material impact

Extra-ordinary items of income/expenditure of material impact

Miscellaneous income which exceeds 1% of total turnover/gross income of organisation or Rs. 50000/-whichever is higher.

Miscellaneous expenses which exceeds 1% of total turnover/gross income of organisation or Rs. 50000/-whichever is higher

Rounding off the figure

Less than 1 lakh- hundred

1 lakh or more but less than 1 crore- thousand

1 crore or more but less than 100 crore-Lakh

100 crore or more but less than 1000 crore- crore

Notes and Instructions for the Schedules

Corpus/Capital Fund (Sch1)

Similar to Capital, Share Capital or Owner’s Fund

It comprises of amounts received by way of contribution specifically to corpus.

It increases or decreases by net operating result as shown in Income & Expenditure A/c.

Opening balance, addition to, deletion and closing balance is shown there.

Addition to corpus shall be net of transfer, if any, to any reserve or earmarked fund.

secs.title: Section 4: Capital Reserve (Sch. 2)
secs.text:
Capital Reserve (Sch. 2)

It shall not include any amount regarded as free for distribution through Income and Expenditure A/c

Surplus on revaluation should be treated as Capital Reserves and shown separately.

Revaluation Reserve (S-2)

Fixed are generally recorded at historical cost

To reflect the effect of changing prices, assets may be revalued by competent Valuer.

Upward revaluation is shown as Revaluation Reserve

It is an unrealised gain and NOT to be shown in Income & Expenditure Accounts

Special Reserve (S-2)

It is created in pursuant to any statutory or regulatory requirement.

General Reserve (S-2)

Any reserve other than Capital Reserve and Revaluation Reserve and special reserve, if any.

Reserve shall not include any amount written off or retained by way of providing for depreciation, renewal or diminution in value of assets or retained by way of providing for any known liability.

Earmarked Fund (Sch. 3)

Amount received as grant/assistance or retained by the entity to be utilised for specific or earmarked purposes.

Amount remains to be utilised for specific purposes shall be disclosed under this head.

The Plan fund received from Central and State Government are to be shown as distinct category of fund.

Records relating to fixed assets acquired/constructed should be maintained for each earmarked fund. However, in financial statement, aggregate accumulated cost up-to each year and of each earmarked fund, unless the assets are taken over, may be disclosed.

Secured Loan & Borrowing (Sch.4)

Secured loan and borrowing shall be such as are against hypothecation/charge/pledge on the asset of the entity.

Loan and borrowing include refinance from institutions and agencies and liability against participation certificate.

Interest accrued and due shall be included under this head.

Interest accrued but not due shall NOT be included under this head but shall be shown as part of current liabilities.

Amount due within a period of less than 12 months as at the Balance Sheet date  need to be disclosed

Un-Secured Loan & Borrowing (Sch.4)

Un-secured loans and borrowings comprise amounts in respect of which no asset of the entity is charged as security or encumbered.

Interest accrued and due shall be included under this head.

Interest accrued but not due shall NOT be included under this head but shall be shown as part of current liabilities.

Amount due within a period of less than 12 months as at the Balance Sheet date  need to be disclosed

Deferred Credit Liabilities (Sch. 5)

Acceptance and other similar long-term obligations in respect of acquisition of assets, the liability for payment of which falls in period longer than 12 months as at the date of balance sheet should be included here

Amount due within a period of less than 12 months as at the Balance Sheet date should separately be disclosed

Current Liabilities which fall due within a relatively shorter period i.e. normally not more than 12 months.

Acceptance

Drawer’s assent on bills of exchange to the order of the drawer.

Sundry Creditor

Amount owned by the entity in favour of others on accounts of goods purchased or services rendered or in respect of contractual obligations

Advance

Amounts received in respect of which goods or services have yet to be supplied or rendered. It includes advance subscription.

Interest accrued but not due

Interest accrued up to the year-end but not due shall be included under the appropriate class of loans & borrowing i.e. secured or unsecured.

Statutory liabilities

Include unpaid liability for TDS under Income Tax Act 1961,Statutory bonus, provident fund, gratuity, ESI and interest on overdue sales tax, excise etc.

Other current liabilities

Amount not covered any sub-head of current liabilities.

Overdraft is an example.

Assets (Fixed Assets)

Land

Freehold- where immovable properties are purchase or acquired by paying a composite cost. Reliable estimate should be made and shown separately.

Leasehold-amortised over the period of lease unless the lease is in perpetuity.

Buildings

Distinction to be made between factory and office building for the purpose of provision for depreciation at different rates

Building premises shall be those which are intended to be wholly or partially used for the purpose of the activities of the entity and would not include Investment Properties

Superstructures on leasehold lands should be depreciated to be co-terminus with amortisation of land unless the superstructures have a shorter life

Building shall include roads, bridges and culverts

Library Books

Where there is a very large number of library books or where there is an established library, these books may be disclosed as a separate category of assets.

Library books will include books/journals/information stored in CD ROMs

Capital-in-Progress

Fixed assets in the course of construction should be shown against this head till they are ready for the intended use.

Plant, machinery and equipment acquired and pending installation should be shown here.

Where sums have been written up for any assets due to their revaluation, the basis thereof should be disclosed. Every balance sheet after the first balance sheet subsequent to the revaluation should show the revised figures for a period of 5 years with the date and amount of revision.

secs.title: Section 5: Where grants relating to specific fixed assets are received and t
secs.text:
Where grants relating to specific fixed assets are received and these are equal to the whole cost of the asset, the fixed assets should be shown in the balance sheet a nominal value.

Grants relatable to depreciable fixed assets may be treated as a deferred income and recognised in the Income and Expenditure account on a systematic and rational basis over the useful life of such assets. In other words such grants should be allocated to the Income over the period and in the proportion in which depreciation is charged.

Grants relatable to non-depreciable assets should be credited to Capital Reserve unless there are pre-conditions requiring fulfilment.

Current Assets, Loans and Advances

Interest accrued on interest bearing staff loans should be accounted notwithstanding that actual recoveries of interest might commence after repayment of principal.

Income from Sale/Service

Sales comprise the aggregate amount for which sales are effected. These would be shown net of trade discount, rebate and returns

Sales are complete when significant risks and rewards of ownership get transferred from the seller to the buyer irrespective of the time of payment or delivery of goods.

Disclosure of exports sale should be made separately

Income must be shown at gross figure and Tax Deducted at Source should be indicated separately.

Other Income

Sales proceeds/realisation, net of book value of the assets shall, if a surplus be included under this sub-head.

Export incentives claimed and not realised up-to the year-end shall not be included in income

Items of material amounts included in Miscellaneous Income should be disclosed separately.

secs.title: Section 1: Assets
secs.text:
Assets

Assets

A resource that a business owns or control as a result of past events and from which future economic value/benefits are expected to flow to the enterprise.

Properties of an asset

Ownership

Economic Value

Resources

That can be eventually turned into cash and cash equivalent

Can be exchanged or sold

Can be used to generate future economic benefits

TYPES OF ASSETS

Convertibility

Physical Existence

Usage

Current

Non-current

Tangible

Intangible

Operating

Non-Operating

Current Assets

Asset that can be easily converted into cash and cash equivalent, generally within a year.

The current assets are also termed as liquid assets.

Cash and cash equivalent, current investment, short-term loan and advances, debtor, Bills receivable, Inventories and other current assets

Non-current

Asset that cannot be easily converted into cash and cash equivalent, generally within a year.

Also known as Long-term Assets or Fixed term assets

Building, Plant, Machinery, Land, Goodwill, Trademarks, Patent, Long-term Loan and advances, Non-current investments, Deferred Tax Assets (Net)

Tangible Assets

Assets that have physical presence.

Cash, Stock, Bonds, Property, Buildings, Machinery, Inventory, Precious Metal and arts.

Non-current tangible assets/fixed assets are recorded in DEAD STOCK REGISTER

Intangible Assets

Assets that have no physical presence.

Patents, Goodwill, Copyright, Brand, Permits, Trade Secret, Trademarks and Corporate Intellectual Property.

Hard to determine the value of such assets.

Operating Assets

Assets that are required in daily operation of a business.

Such assets are required to generate revenue

Cash, Stock, Building, Machinery, Plant, Equipment, Patents, Copyright and Goodwill etc.

Non-Operating Assets

Assets that are not required in daily operation of a business.

Such assets generate revenue

Short-term Investment, Marketable Securities, Vacant Land and interest from fixed deposit etc.

Some Others Assets

Biological Assets

International Accounting Standard 41 (IAS 41) defines biological asset as a living animal or plant but NON-HUMAN

Common examples are animals and plants. Animals such as goats, sheep, cows, buffalos, calves and fish and plants such as vegetables, crops, tress and fruit orchards

Animals such as dogs, horse, pigeons and other animals used for racing and also those used in theme parks such as pony rides are not treated as biological assets.

Biological assets keep on transforming and so they grow, degenerate and produce.

Quantitative and qualitative changes occur in the nature of biological assets called biological transformation

Biological assets should be recognised in Balance sheet and Income statements

Should be recognised at Fair value minus point of sale cost/harvest.

Wasting Assets

Assets the value of which declines over multiple of time period.

Examples are natural resources such as mineral, oils, natural gas

Such assets are eventually used to last and then have no remaining value

Floating Assets

Assets value of which may change depending on day to day transactions.

Examples are Cash, stock

Fictitious Assets

Fictitious Assets are not assets in true sense.

They are the expenses and losses which could not be written off during the accounting period of their incidence.

Unlike other assets which provide economic benefits in the future , fictitious assets are an outcome of an activity in the past

Examples are Preliminary expenses to float a business, promotional expenses of a business, discount allowed on issue of shares and losses on issue of debentures.

Cost of Fixed Assets

At the acquisition cost inclusive of inward freight, duties and taxes and incidental and direct expenses related to acquisition.

In respect of project involving construct, related pre-operational expenses including interest on specific loan prior to construction form part of cost of assets

Fixed assets received by way of non-monetary grant/other than towards corpus fund are capitalised at value stated by corresponding credit to capital reserve.

Library Books

Where there is a very large number of library books or where there is an established library, these books may be disclosed as a separate category of assets.

Library books will include books/journals/information stored in CD ROMs

Liabilities

Liabilities

are obligations or debts that an enterprise has to pay at some time in the future.

In other words liabilities are future sacrifices of economic benefits that an entity is required to make to other entities as a result of past events or transactions.

TYPES OF LIABILITIES

Current/short-term Liabilities

Non-current/Long Term Liabilities

Contingent Liabilities

Current Liabilities

Debts or obligations that need to be repaid within a year.

Current liabilities should be watched carefully by the entity to ensure that it possessed enough liquidity from current assets to guarantee.

Examples are Accounts payable, Bills payable, interest payable, income tax payable, bank overdraft, accrued expenses, short-term loan, short-term provision

Current liabilities are used as a key components in several short-term liquidity measures

Non-Current Liabilities

Debts or obligations that need to be repaid over a year.

It is the important source of the long-term financing of a business entity.

Companies take on long-term debts to acquire immediate capital to fund the purchase of capital assets or invest in new capital projects.

secs.title: Section 2: Examples are Bonds payable, Long-term Loan and Advances, Deferred
secs.text:
Examples are Bonds payable, Long-term Loan and Advances, Deferred tax liabilities, Mortgage payable, Capital lease, Debenture

Contingent Liabilities

Liabilities that may occur depending on the outcome of a FUTURE event

These are also termed as Potential Liabilities.

Examples are Lawsuits, product Warranties, Discounting of a bill till it is honoured or dishonoured.

Secured Loan & Borrowing (Sch.4)

Secured loan and borrowing shall be such as are against hypothecation/charge/pledge on the asset of the entity.

Loan and borrowing include refinance from institutions and agencies and liability against participation certificate.

Interest accrued and due shall be included under this head.

Interest accrued but not due shall NOT be included under this head but shall be shown as part of current liabilities.

Amount due within a period of less than 12 months as at the Balance Sheet date  need to be disclosed

Un-Secured Loan & Borrowing (Sch.4)

Un-secured loans and borrowings comprise amounts in respect of which no asset of the entity is charged as security or encumbered.

Interest accrued and due shall be included under this head.

Interest accrued but not due shall NOT be included under this head but shall be shown as part of current liabilities.

Amount due within a period of less than 12 months as at the Balance Sheet date  need to be disclosed

Deferred Credit Liabilities

Acceptance and other similar long-term obligations in respect of acquisition of assets, the liability for payment of which falls in period longer than 12 months as at the date of balance sheet should be included here

Discount

Discount

The deduction in the price of the goods sold. In other words, the certain amount of money determined at a fixed rate and deducted from invoice price or amount received is called the discount.

TYPES OF DISCOUNT

Trade Discount

Quantity Discount

Cash Discount

Trade Discount

The amount which is deducted from the PRICE LIST of the goods sold is called trade discount.

The seller fixes up the invoice price or sale price deducting trade discount from the listed price.

Trade discount is not accounted for

Quantitative Discount

The discount allowed by the seller to the buyer on the amount crossing the minimum target sale is called quantitative discount

In other words, after granting normal trade discount, if the sale amount crosses the minimum target sale, the seller grants an additional discount to the buyer.

It is included in the cash discount which is shown on the challan or invoice.

Cash Discount

The seller grants some amount as discount to the debtors if the debtor pay the amount within the stipulated period or earlier.

This is also called the early payment discount.

DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TRADE AND CASH DISCOUNT

Point of Difference

Trade Discount

Cash Discount

Deduction

From the listed price list

From the invoiced price

Allowed

To bulk buyers

To buyer for prompt payment

Base

Catalogue price list

Invoice price

Concern

Arises out of trading

Arises out of debts settlement

Opportunity

For buyer to earn reasonable profit

Save by paying in time

Accounting

Not accounted for either of Seller or buyer

accounted for both Seller or buyer

Company

Company

an incorporated association of persons created by law to carry on the expressly laid down objectives

A company exists on in the contemplation of law.

It may be formed by an act of parliament, or by Royal Charter or by registration under the company law

A company has perpetual existence i.e. the existence of a company can only be terminated by law and not by the death, retirement, insanity of its members.

TYPES OF COMPANY

Statutory Company

A company formed by a special Act passed either by the central or the state legislature.

These companies are governed by the provisions of their special Acts

The object such companies are not to as such earn profits but to serve people

The audit of such companies is conducted under the supervision, control and guidance of the CAG

Some important statutory companies are Reserve Bank of India, State Bank of India, Life Insurance Corporation of India, industrial Finance Corporation etc.

Registered Company

Company registered under the Indian Companies Act

These companies are governed and regulated by the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.

They may be limited by shares or limited by guarantee or unlimited companies.

KINDS OF COMPANIES ON THE BASIS OF LIABILITY OF MEMBERS

Cos. limited by shares

This is a company having the liability of its members limited by the memorandum to the amount unpaid on the shares respectively held by them

The last word of the name of such companies should be “Limited”

A large majority of the companies registered in India belong to this category

For example, if AB Ltd. has a share capital of 10,000 shares of Rs. 10 each, and A has purchased 100 shares on which he has paid so far Rs. 6 per share, the maximum liability of A is only Rs. 4 per share.

Company limited by Guarantee

This is a company in which the liability of each member is limited to such amount as the members may voluntarily undertake under the memorandum to contribute to meet out the deficiency of the assets of the company in the event of its being wound up

Such companies may or may not have share capital.

If it has share capital, the liability of the members becomes two-fold; firstly, the amount unpaid on the shares held by them and secondly, amount payable under the guarantee.

secs.title: Section 3: Unlimited companies
secs.text:
Unlimited companies

A company not having any limit towards the liability of its members is an unlimited company.

The liability extends to the whole amount of the company’s debts and liabilities.

The registered companies (whether limited or unlimited) may be either private or public companies.

Private limited company

Private limited company is held by few individuals privately having separate legal entity.

In this the shareholders cannot trade shares publicly. Shareholders cannot sell their shares without the approval of other shareholders

It is a company which restricts the right of its members to transfer its shares and it doesn’t send invitation to the public for subscription of its shares

Public Company

A public limited company is a form of business organization that operates as a separate legal entity from its owners.

It is formed and owned by shareholders.

Shares of a public limited company are listed and traded at a stock exchange market freely

DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A PRIVATE & PUBLIC LIMITED COMPANY

Feature

Private Limited Company

Public Limited Company

Member

Minimum 2 Maximum 200

Minimum 3 Maximum Unlimited

Index of member

No need to keep an index of members

Need to keep an index of members

Director

Minimum 2 Maximum 15 (at-least 1 director stays in India for 182 days)

Minimum 3 Maximum 15

Private Director

No need to appoint a private director

Need to appoint a private director

Invitation to Public

No allowed. So no need to issue prospectus

Allowed. So need to issue prospectus

Paid-up Capital

1 Lakh

5 Lakh

Quorum at AGM

2

5

Commencement of business

Not Mandatory

Certificate to this effect is mandatory

Name

word private limited after its name

word limited after its name

Managerial Remuneration

Up-to 11% of net profit

No restriction

Statutory meeting

Not Mandatory

Mandatory

Audit Committee

Audit Committee on a Board is not mandatory

Audit Committee on a Board is mandatory

One Person Company

This is a type of company that has only one member.

Such companies provide the benefits of both forms of business- Proprietorship and Company.

With formation of an OPC business can be run in the same way as a proprietorship by complying with law and keeping the liability of the member limited by shares or guarantee.

Provisions of OPC under Companies Act 2013

Treatment

All the provisions of the Act applicable to private companies shall also be applicable to OPC unless otherwise excluded from compliance.

It should be treated as a private company for all legal purposes.

Director

Minimum 1 Maximum 15

Name

The name of the company shall include the words ‘One Person Company’ within brackets below the name of the company.

Nominee

The person forming an OPC has to nominate a person with that person’s written consent as a nominee of the OPC

HOLDING AND SUBSIDIARY COMPANY

A company which controls another company is called a Holding Company and the company so controlled is called a Subsidiary Company.

A company shall be deemed to control another company in the following cases

Board of Director

controls the majority composition of the board of directors of another company

Share Capital

MORE THAN ONE-HALF of the total share capital either at its own or together with one or more of its subsidiary companies

subsidiary of the subsidiary

If another company is a subsidiary of the first mentioned company’s subsidiary

ASSOCIATE COMPANY

“Associate Company” as in relation to another company, means a company in which that other company has a significant influence, but which is not a subsidiary company of the company having such influence and includes a Joint Venture Company.

“Significant Influence” means control of AT-LEAST 20% of total share capital BUT LESS THAN 50% of share capital by another company, or control of business decisions under an agreement.

SMALL COMPANY

Small company means a company, other than a public company, whose-

1. Paid-up share capital doesn’t exceed ₹ 50 lakhs or such higher amount as may be prescribed.

2. Turnover of which as per its last P&L A/C doesn’t exceed ₹ 2 crore or such higher amount as may be prescribed.

Not a Small company

A holding or a subsidiary company

A company registered under section 8 of the 2013 Act

A company or body corporate governed under any special Act

Exemption to Small Company

Cash Flow Statement

Financial Statement may not include cash flow statement

Filling on annual return

Director and Company Secretary. When no company secretary by two director

Meeting

At-least one meeting of Board of director in each half of a CALENDAR YEAR.

Government company

means any company in which not less than 51% of the share capital is held by the by the Government(s).

It also includes a company which is a subsidiary of a Government company.

Special Provision

Audit

Auditor (CA) shall be appointed or reappointed by the Central Government on the advice of the CAG

CAG shall also have the power to conduct a supplementary test audit of the company’s account by persons appointed by him

The auditor is required to submit a copy of his audit report to the CAG, who shall have the right to comment upon the report

Preparation & Submission

Where the Central Government is a member of a Government Company, the Central Government shall prepare an annual report on the working and affairs of the company within 3 months of its annual general meeting before which the audit report is placed.

secs.title: Section 4: The annual report is to be laid before both houses of Parliament
secs.text:
The annual report is to be laid before both houses of Parliament together with a copy of the audit report

Foreign Company

a company incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode and

Conducts any business activity in India in any other manner.

Producer Company

It means a body corporate having objects or activities specified in section 581B and deals primarily with the produce of its active Members for carrying out one or more of the eleven items specified in the Act.

DORMANT COMPANY

Where a company is formed and registered under this Act for a future project or to hold an asset or intellectual property and has no significant accounting transaction, such a company or an inactive company may make an application to the Registrar in such manner as may be prescribed for obtaining the status of a dormant company.

Inactive company means a company which has not been carrying on any business or operation, or has not made any significant accounting transaction during the last 2 financial years, or has not filed financial statements and annual returns during the last 2 financial years.

Survey & Write-off with respect to Govt. Departments

Power to write off of losses are available under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules, 1978.

Losses due to depreciation

Losses not due to depreciation

Normal fluctuation of market prices

losses due to theft or fraud

normal wear and tear

losses due to neglect

lack of foresight in regulating purchases

anticipated losses on account of obsolescence of stores or of purchases in excess of requirements

negligence after purchase

losses due to damage

losses due to extra ordinary situations under ‘Force Majeure’ like fire, flood, enemy action, etc.

STANDING SURVEY COMMITTEE

The Head of the Department shall constitute a Standing Survey Committee (SSC) for a period of 3 years

It should necessarily have one or two members from outside the department.

The committee should also have one or two supervisory staff who are experts and who are fully aware about the items for disposal.

The survey must be carried out in the presence of at least five members of the Standing Survey Committee (SSC), so constituted, including one external member.
